facts.text: This project demonstrates reinforcement learning for robotic tasks using ROS 2 Humble, Gazebo, Stable-Baselines3 and Gymnasium.
start_learning registers RacingBotEnv-v0 with entry point rl_racing.gazebo_env:GazeboEnv and max_episode_steps=1000.
GazeboEnv subclasses GazeboConnection (from rl_racing.gazebo_connections) and gymnasium's Env.
GazeboConnection subclasses rclpy's Node, and its constructor creates the node gazebo_connection.
The action space is Box(low=[-1, -1], high=[1, 1], dtype=float32).
The observation space is Box(low=0, high=1, shape=(60,), dtype=float32).
The environment sets max_linear_vel=1.0, min_linear_vel=0.0, angular_vel=1.0 and min_obstacle_dist=0.2.
seed() creates a generator with gymnasium.utils.seeding.np_random and returns [seed].
spin() clears done_laser_ and done_odom_ and calls rclpy.spin_once(self) in a loop, with no deadline, until both flags are set.
step() applies the action, spins, reads the observation, evaluates done, computes the reward and returns (obs, reward, done, False, {}).
reset() optionally seeds, calls resetSim(), updates the episode, spins, reads the observation, clears last_action and returns (obs, {}).

_set_action computes the linear velocity (max_linear_vel * (action[0] + 1) + min_linear_vel * (1 - action[0])) / 2 and the angular velocity (angular_vel * (action[1] + 1) - angular_vel * (1 - action[1])) / 2, then calls publish_velocity.
_get_obs returns the laser scan divided by 10.
_is_done is true when any laser distance is below min_obstacle_dist.

The reward is 5 * get_current_linear_vel(), plus -(min_obstacle_dist - min(obs)) when the minimum of the scaled observation is below min_obstacle_dist, minus 20 when done, plus 0.1, and minus 2 when the action equals last_action.
GazeboConnection publishes geometry_msgs/Twist on /cmd_vel and subscribes to nav_msgs/Odometry on /odom and sensor_msgs/LaserScan on /front_laser/scan.
publish_velocity puts velocity[0] in linear.x and velocity[1] in angular.z.
laser_callback copies msg.ranges into a numpy array and replaces infinite readings with 10.
odom_callback stores msg.twist.twist.linear.x as the current linear velocity.

resetSim repeats wait_for_service(max_retry_) until /reset_simulation is available, sends an Empty request, waits with rclpy.spin_until_future_complete without a timeout and sets resetSim_done_ when the future has a result.
The GazeboConnection docstring lists /reset_simulation, /reset_world, /pause_physics and /unpause_physics under 'Services not used'.
The documented simulation launch is ros2 launch sim_package start_simulation.launch.py.
The documented training launch is ros2 launch rl_racing start_training.launch.py.
The package declares rclpy, geometry_msgs, sensor_msgs, nav_msgs, std_srvs, gymnasium, numpy and stable_baselines3 dependencies.
The URDF attaches a front_laser link to the chassis at x=0.125, z=0.25.
The racing_track world includes model://td_robot at pose 0 5 0.01.

The td_robot model's laser sensor has 60 horizontal samples from -1.5708 to 1.5708, a range of 0.1 to 10 and an update rate of 100, and its libgazebo_ros_ray_sensor plugin remaps its output to /front_laser/scan as sensor_msgs/LaserScan.
The td_robot model's libgazebo_ros_diff_drive plugin uses command_topic cmd_vel and odometry_topic odom with max_wheel_torque 20, max_wheel_acceleration 1.8 and update_rate 50.

determinism.notes: this package's fake is deterministic for a given seed and action sequence: the seed selects the placeholder starting clearance.  The upstream reset(seed) only creates np_random (gazebo_env.py:34-36) and no code consumes that generator, so it does not seed the Gazebo world; the two implementations do not produce the same trajectory

gaps: the checked fake is a pure Python kinematic stand-in for Gazebo: it models no rigid-body physics, contacts, wheels, motor, laser ray casting, odometry, sensor noise or rendering; its 60-beam scan is a placeholder profile around one scalar clearance and was never compared with a Gazebo run

the world includes model://td_robot (sim_package/worlds/racing_track.world:31-35), whose SDF carries the 60-sample, 0.1 to 10 laser that publishes /front_laser/scan and the diff-drive plugin on cmd_vel and odom (sim_package/models/td_robot/td_robot.sdf:340-366, 727-750); the URDF has only the front_laser link; the fake models neither plugin
the fake has no physical timestep or wall-clock pacing: fidelity.timestep_ms is 0 and a cap.world.step.v1 tick is one fake control transition, not one Gazebo physics step

the upstream reset calls the /reset_simulation service and spin() waits for both a laser and an odometry message (gazebo_env.py:38-42,62-72); the fake returns immediately, does not use ROS and does not prove that a Gazebo reset completed

the upstream step publishes a Twist and waits for one laser and one odometry message; the fake instead applies its own placeholder clearance update, so its trajectories are not comparable with the upstream simulator

the upstream observation space declares 60 beams and the model's laser has 60 samples and a 10 maximum range; the fake always returns 60 placeholder values and does not model readings below the 0.1 minimum range

the upstream is not lockstep: Gazebo runs freely between steps, and a step publishes one Twist and then waits, with no deadline, for the next laser and odometry messages (gazebo_env.py:38-60); a paused or silent simulator blocks it, and reset waits without a timeout for /reset_simulation (gazebo_connections.py:68-82)

constructing the upstream environment needs a prior global rclpy.init() and creates the node gazebo_connection; close() destroys that node and never calls rclpy.shutdown; RacingBotEnv-v0 is registered only inside start_learning.main with max_episode_steps=1000, so gymnasium.make in the server finds no such environment, and a registered one would be truncated after 1000 steps, which the fake does not do
the upstream progress reward reads the odometry linear velocity (gazebo_connections.py:61-66); the fake has no odometry and uses the commanded linear velocity instead

the upstream safety penalty compares the observation scaled by 1/10 with min_obstacle_dist 0.2, which the crash test applies to unscaled ranges, so the penalty starts at ten times the crash distance; the fake copies this as written

the README's documented training launch (start_training.launch.py) runs the upstream TD3 trainer, which builds its own environment and publishes /cmd_vel itself; it must not run beside an MHS deployment of this environment
no live ROS 2 or Gazebo backend was run and no hardware is declared; the package only serves the fake backend, and the upstream environment needs ROS 2 Humble, Gazebo and the robot model

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: Software latch only: after an e-stop the bridge refuses step and reset until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch, and the fake's state is kept and stays readable. Nothing is sent to the environment: a live Gazebo is free-running and would keep simulating with the last /cmd_vel Twist in place, because the upstream publishes velocity only from step and calls no pause service. The latch does not publish a zero Twist, so a physical base subscribed to /cmd_vel is not stopped.
